re_line: Xi state visit, $30 billion tariff cuts, Taiwan arms package, China and Iran, Congress on Chinese tech
editors_note: Xi's Washington visit produced a two-month truce extension, $30 billion in reciprocal tariff cuts and a November AI dialogue. Export controls, AI governance and Taiwan were left unresolved.

week_at_a_glance.headline: Golden Week ends Oct. 7 with fuel exports suspended
week_at_a_glance.body: Chinese refiners suspended October fuel exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau, and PetroChina cancelled some gasoline and jet-fuel cargoes on Sept. 30, Reuters reported. Lianhe Zaobao reported it is unclear whether Beijing will resume approvals after the holiday ends Oct. 7.

week_at_a_glance.headline: Busan-deal suspensions set to expire around Nov. 10
week_at_a_glance.body: Rare-earth and yttrium export controls remain a live flashpoint ahead of the roughly Nov. 10 expiration of last year's Busan-deal suspensions, the Wall Street Journal reported. The Journal charted U.S. countermeasures including tariffs, stockpiling and domestic-production subsidies.

week_at_a_glance.headline: Trump to meet Xi in China during APEC Shenzhen
week_at_a_glance.body: Trump said he will travel to China in November to meet Xi again, Reuters reported. The trip would coincide with the APEC summit in Shenzhen.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Senate delays Chinese car ban until after midterms
heard_on_the_hill.body: The Senate punted a bill that would permanently ban Chinese-made cars from the U.S. market until after the Nov. 3 midterm elections, AP reported. Reuters reported senators plan to bring the measure up again for a vote in November.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Senate bill would bar Chinese optical modules
heard_on_the_hill.body: A bipartisan Senate group proposed legislation banning Chinese-made optical modules from federal national-security systems, with a five-year grace period, Jiemian reported. Chinese optical and communications stocks sold off sharply on Monday, with the ChiNext index down 4.53 percent.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Lawmakers move to bar Chinese datacenter technology
heard_on_the_hill.body: Members of Congress are moving to keep Chinese-origin datacenter hardware and software out of sensitive U.S. government systems, Reuters reported. The push follows warnings that Chinese AI models and cloud infrastructure could pose data-security risks to federal networks.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Wicker says U.S. must honor Taiwan commitments
heard_on_the_hill.body: Senate Armed Services Committee Chairman Roger Wicker said Washington's security commitments to Taiwan must be upheld after meeting Taiwan's representative to the U.S., Alexander Yui, the Taipei Times reported. Four other Republican senators called on the administration to release more than $14 billion in stalled Taiwan security assistance.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Johnson rejects claims arms package is trade leverage
heard_on_the_hill.body: House Speaker Mike Johnson said Taiwan's stability is important to U.S. national security and the economy, and dismissed suggestions that a delayed $14 billion arms package is being used as leverage in trade talks, the Taipei Times reported. He said Trump will have completed roughly $40 billion in Taiwan arms sales across two terms.

in_the_news.headline: China, U.S. agree $30 billion reciprocal tariff cut, new AI dialogue after Xi's Washington visit
in_the_news.body: China's foreign ministry said the Sept. 23-25 summit produced an eight-point consensus, including $30 billion in reciprocal tariff relief and an AI dialogue due in November, Reuters reported. AP reported the sides agreed to an AI-incident channel, and Bloomberg reported China committed to importing at least 10 million metric tons of U.S. coal annually in 2027 and 2028.

in_the_news.headline: Xi presses Trump to 'oppose' Taiwan independence
in_the_news.body: Xi pressed Trump to "oppose" Taiwan independence at their Sept. 24 White House meeting, Bloomberg reported, and Reuters reported Taiwan's government accused Xi of "distorting facts." AP reported a $14 billion arms package remains stalled, while Trump said only that Xi "knows how I feel" on Taiwan.

in_the_news.headline: Chinese intelligence aids Iran's improved targeting of U.S. forces
in_the_news.body: U.S. intelligence assessments described to CNN by four sources found that satellite imagery and intelligence support from Chinese groups helped Iran strike U.S. military bases with improved precision. Reuters reported Ambassador David Perdue said Trump told Xi that Chinese assistance to Iran was "totally unacceptable" and received assurances.

in_the_news.headline: U.S. officials see Chinese invasion of Taiwan unlikely before 2028
in_the_news.body: U.S. officials believe Beijing is unlikely to use force against Taiwan before 2028, even though Xi has ordered the PLA to be ready to do so by 2027, Reuters reported. Officials pointed to an anti-corruption purge that has slowed PLA readiness and said Beijing may wait for the outcome of Taiwan's 2028 election.

in_the_news.headline: China cuts tariffs on U.S. farm goods but excludes soybeans from relief list
in_the_news.body: China published its tariff-cut list under the $30-billion-per-side framework, lowering levies on U.S. farm goods, cosmetics and medical devices but leaving soybeans off, Reuters reported. Nikkei reported rare earths stayed off both countries' lists, and Reuters reported China's soybean purchases remain weak despite a pledge to buy at least $17 billion a year of U.S. farm goods.

research_roundup.headline: What did the Trump-Xi summit actually accomplish?
research_roundup.body: Brookings asks "What did the Trump-Xi summit actually accomplish?" in a review of the Washington visit.

research_roundup.headline: Trump Had the Chance to Address U.S.-China AI Safety. He Threw Xi a Party Instead.
research_roundup.body: Carnegie argues that "Trump had the chance to address U.S.-China AI safety" at the summit and "threw Xi a party instead."

research_roundup.headline: The Limits of Trump and Xi’s Photo-Op Summit
research_roundup.body: CFR examines "the limits of Trump and Xi's photo-op summit."

research_roundup.headline: The Trump-Xi Summit Leaves Taiwan in Limbo
research_roundup.body: CNAS argues that "the Trump-Xi summit leaves Taiwan in limbo."

research_roundup.headline: How do we deal with Chinese overcapacity?
research_roundup.body: PIIE takes up the question of how to deal with Chinese overcapacity.
